answer: Require each agent to prove counterparty diversity: a genuine agent wanders through many independent counterparties over weeks, while a sybil farm keeps its identities trading inside one closed grove of sock-puppets. The protocol scores how widely an agent's interaction graph spreads and demands a minimum number of distinct, unrelated peers before rewards unlock. Faking it means cultivating real relationships across the whole garden of the economy for every fake identity — slow, costly, and easy to spot when the graph stays cliquish.
